I am a CS student specializing in C++, data structures, and competitive programming. I enjoy breaking down complex challenges into efficient, structured code.

Our team is analytical, disciplined, and ready to turn ambitious ideas into functional projects for the Space Apps Challenge. We are fully covered on the backend and technical side, but we are open to connecting with anyone skilled in UI/UX design or data visualization to help bring our concepts to life visually!
summary:
Space Walkie Talkie is an innovative interactive desktop application developed in C++ (C++20) using SFML 2.6.1 that transforms complex NASA Earth observation datasets—specifically global sea surface currents and temperature image frames—into immersive soundscapes.

The project directly addresses the challenge by bridging hard science and accessibility through data sonification. By loading satellite images into memory and scanning individual pixel arrays, our custom audio engine dynamically maps pixel brightness and saturation to audio frequencies and amplitudes, generating real-time PCM sound buffers paired with a space-themed graphical interface.

This is critically important because it redefines how we interact with environmental science. By turning visual satellite data into a multi-sensory musical experience, the project fosters inclusive science communication—making complex oceanographic patterns engaging for a broad audience while opening up accessible Earth science exploration for blind and visually impaired individuals who rely on auditory cues.
details: Space Walkie Talkie is an interactive desktop application developed in C++ (C++20) using CMake and SFML 2.6.1 (Simple and Fast Multimedia Library) that transforms complex NASA Earth observation data—specifically global sea surface currents and temperature datasets—into immersive soundscapes. By loading satellite images into memory and parsing their pixel arrays, a custom procedural audio engine calculates individual pixel brightness and color saturation values to dynamically map visual data points to audio frequencies and amplitudes for real-time PCM sound buffer synthesis. Wrapped in an interactive, space-themed graphical user interface featuring animated visual elements and live waveform visualizers, the project bridges hard science and art to foster inclusive science communication and accessible, multi-sensory Earth science exploration.
